title: Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cell Isolation and Stimulation
author: Dorota Kmiec
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.r7cd9iw
materials: Bring all reagents and the centrifuge (Eppendorf 5810R) to a room temperature.

steps.title: Dilute Buffy Coat
steps.instruction: Dilute buffy coat (Deutsches Rotes Kreuz, DRK) 1:4 with DPBS (Gibco).

steps.title: Prepare Separation Tube
steps.instruction: Add 20ml of Biocoll separating solution (Merck, cat# L6115) into a 50 ml plastic tube.

steps.title: Layer and Centrifuge Buffy Coat
steps.instruction: Slowly pipette 20ml of diluted buffy coat over the Biocoll solution without mixing the layers, then centrifuge at 1200 RCF for 20 min with the brake switched off.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs
steps.instruction: Transfer the white interface containing PBMCs to a new 50ml tube.

steps.title: Wash PBMCs
steps.instruction: Wash the PBMCs twice using DPBS.

substeps.instruction: Add DPBS up to a total volume of 40ml and centrifuge at 1400rpm for 5min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 40ml of DPBS.

steps.title: Resuspend Cells in Medium
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 10ml of RPMI1640 supplemented with 2 mM L-glutamine, 100 µg/ml streptomycin, 100 units/ml penicillin, and 10 % (v/v) heat inactivated FCS (Gibco).

steps.title: Adjust Cell Concentration
steps.instruction: Adjust the cell concentration to 2,000,000 cells/ml by adding more medium.

steps.title: Stimulate PBMCs
steps.instruction: Stimulate the cells and incubate for 3 days at 37°C, 5%CO2.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µg/ml PHA (Murex) and 10 ng/ml IL-2 (Sigma-Ark).
If cells adhere to the walls of the flask, remove them by gentle pipetting.
